key_insight: The paper shows that superconducting grid-state qubits can achieve repeat-until-success state preparation and improved measurement so that combined SPAM error falls below 10^-3.
engineering_relevance: This pushes bosonic quantum error correction closer to practical fault-tolerant hardware by making grid-state qubits competitive with transmon-level calibration and readout performance.
method: Repeat-until-success preparation of cardinal and magic states
Measurement protocol that corrects finite-energy envelope and auxiliary-qubit readout errors
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experimentally achieved combined state-preparation and measurement error below 10^-3, about two orders of magnitude better than prior state of the art.
watch_item: Results are promising, but scaling will still depend on maintaining these low SPAM errors under larger circuits, more modes, and device-specific loss and calibration drift.
paper_title: Quantum error correction of a grid-state qubit with state preparation and measurement errors below $10^{-3}$
